not_mined: Front matter, acknowledgements, table of contents and abbreviations (lines 1-317): no claims, apart from the contents used to locate chapters.

Ch. 1 s.1-2: detail on Delmedigo's bibliographies and library inventories (lines ~873-905, 1198-1229): only the kabbalah list, the dating of the letter and the library-not-read points were taken; footnote-only bibliography not mined.

Ch. 2: First and Second Exposition details (physics, the ten spheres, the elemental and planetary correspondences, lines ~1559-1700, 1801-1925) summarised in two or three architectural claims; the taxonomy of the fifteen relationships in the Sixth Exposition (lines 2609-2730) not itemised.

Ch. 3 s.1 (lines ~3038-3745): fifteenth-century reception of the fourfold method, Glossa and Postilla circulation, humanist philology (Manetti, Valla, Erasmus), incunable survey. Not relevant to angelology or the One; only the Apologia's Jewish fourfold scheme, the Aquinas-Dionysius pointer and the absence of Genesis commentaries were taken.

Ch. 3 s.2 (lines ~3830-4100): the Latin and Greek exegetes named in the first proem (Ambrose, Augustine, Bede, Basil, Chrysostom, Philo etc.): only Origen, Albertus and Aegidius, the catena hypothesis and the unresolved identifications were extracted.

Ch. 3 s.3 (lines 4484-4723): the Job manuscript and Psalm philology soundings (Ps. 6, 10, 47) taken only as method; the Hebrew glosses themselves not itemised. The range ends at 4723, the last sentence of the paragraph that straddles line 4700; R-BLACK-B should begin at line 4724 ('Aside from this philological content...').

proposed_topics.label: Pico's life and career as it bears on his writings: Florence, Rome, the trial, Lorenzo, the papal response to the Heptaplus
The authorities Pico names or rejects in the Heptaplus first proem, and how far he knew them directly (catena, Recanati, Bahir)
Delmedigo, Mithridates and Alemanno as channels of Jewish and Arabic learning to Pico; limits of his Hebrew

notes: Cruxes: (1) Ch. 2 s.3, lines 2015-2023 (Third Exposition): Black reports Pico first planned two expositions of the angelic world, Hebrew and Dionysian, kept only the Dionysian and promised a separate book on Jewish doctrine (claim black2006-a:066). Black does not say whether that book was written; nothing in this range answers it. (2) Ch. 1 s.2: Black's stance that Pico could not necessarily read complete kabbalistic treatises (claims 048, 052) and that Recanati (via Mithridates) is the dominant kabbalistic source of the 900; Zohar known only through Recanati (claims 122, 127). (3) Heptaplus architecture: constant Genesis 1.1-27 narrative, changing framework defined at the start of each exposition (claim 059), the 5+1+1 reading via the Trinity (claim 090), and the forty-nine gates (claim 005; developed in ch. 7, outside this range). (4) Pico's own quoted Latin appears only inside Black's footnotes; where I cite it, the warrant is scholar_evidence (Black quoting Pico), never primary_text, because the gate rejects primary_text from a scholarly work. OCR: Hebrew glyphs are dropped, so quotations containing Hebrew words lose them; 'Jo.hanan', 'Mena.hem', 'Ye.zirah' carry stray dots (the gate ignores punctuation; I copied 'Ye.zirah' as it stands because 'Yetzirah' would fail). Two claims have quotes broken by footnotes across page breaks and are given as separate quotations. Not covered: Black's account of Aquinas on Dionysius and the Hebrew angelic hierarchy (chapters 4-5, other packets).
